dossier.architecture: Wide acquisition tunnel plus independently coordinated horizontal extension, vertical elevator, shoulder and claw.

subsystems.intake: Wide overhead cube intake; rollers and star wheels funnel and center cubes. Cones enter through the claw.
subsystems.transfer: Internal cube tunnel feeds a coordinated claw handoff. Interview describes physical room for three pieces; this is not permission to transport three outside the game's protected possession zones.
subsystems.scoring: Belt-driven vertical elevator, chain/rope horizontal extension and articulated arm position the claw.
subsystems.drivetrain: Wide robot footprint deliberately chosen for high-level alliance play; detailed module specification not established here.
subsystems.endgame: Charge-station implementation needs a separate technical reference; the interview concentrates on acquisition and placement.
subsystems.controls: Simultaneous joint motion with collision constraints. Limelight object detection corrects autonomous cone acquisition.

versions: Tipped-cone recovery uses a deliberate uprighting sequence; team preferred reliable station loading as loose cones became less available at high-level play.
dossier.analysis: Study how independent reach and acquisition functions can overlap. The price is joint coordination and collision management; copying the mechanism count without that software capability would miss the architecture's premise.
limits: Full configuration chronology not yet audited.

context_documents.title: 2023-1323 · Buffered cube supply and separate reach axes create an alliance tool
context_documents.body:
# 2023-1323: Buffered cube supply and separate reach axes create an alliance tool

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A wide overhead cube collector funnels through an internal tunnel to a claw. Separate vertical and horizontal elevator axes plus an articulated arm provide reach. The interview distinguishes normal cone pickup from a slower tipped-cone uprighting maneuver.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly describes designing for high-level play and wanting a differentiated capability. The physical room for multiple pieces is not permission to possess them outside the applicable protected zones.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Buffering can decouple human-player delivery from the next placement, but only within the game’s legal possession constraints. Extra reach axes also create collision and maintenance demands. The slower cone fallback is capability, not evidence it is the preferred cycle.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test legal buffered operation, tunnel recovery, both-axis settling and cone fallback cycle cost.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: MadTown 2023 season
source_reviews.facts: Team labels the competition robot ETR 19 and separately describes two COTS-focused CAD concepts intended to help other teams.
source_reviews.limitations: The COTS statement applies to the concept program. This page does not establish ETR 19 drivetrain or superstructure details.

source_reviews.title: 1323 MadTown Robotics | Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the complete interview publisher introduction.
source_reviews.facts: Publisher identifies two elevators, two intakes and object detection.
source_reviews.limitations: Secondary summary. Full interview captions were unavailable.

source_reviews.title: 1323 interview
source_reviews.review_basis: Inherited synopsis. No fresh full-caption or visual review.
source_reviews.facts: Inherited account describes separate cube and cone acquisition, a cube tunnel, vertical lift and horizontal extension, and coordinated motion.
source_reviews.limitations: Treat specific details and configuration dates as provisional.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: ETR 19 coupled a broad cube collection route to a positioning system with several independent motions. In the retained account, the floor cube intake delivers to the same scoring claw that takes cones. The independent axes then position that claw for the grid. This gives the machine the chance to start some motions before others finish, but it makes successful timing and repeatable handoff part of the mechanical architecture. The team’s season page identifies ETR 19 separately from its two shared competition concepts.
piece_flow: Use the wide cube collector and funnel the cube to a transfer pose. The older interview account describes rollers and star wheels guiding it through a tunnel.
Coordinate the claw with the tunnel for cube handoff. For cones, use the claw's direct acquisition route. The inherited account describes a separate recovery move for tipped cones.
Lift, extend and orient to place the piece. The older account describes some joints moving simultaneously within collision limits. Withdraw and make the claw available for the next load.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The tunnel needs enough clearance for cube rotation, guide deflection and release while sitting under or near moving scoring hardware. The claw has to be in position during cube transfer and then be free to leave. Independently driven height and reach improve access to placement poses but occupy space and increase moving mass and electrical demand when accelerating together.

subsystems.name: Cube collector and tunnel
subsystems.construction: The broad double-intake architecture is reported by the publisher. Rollers, star wheels and the tunnel are from the older interview account.
subsystems.operation: Collect a cube at the floor and center it for claw transfer.
subsystems.team_rationale: The older synopsis describes acquisition breadth and a guided handoff. Precise mechanism rationale needs fuller team text.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Measure lateral and angular exit error and use that to set the claw window. A wide entrance is ineffective if off-center cubes jam downstream.
subsystems.interfaces: Collector, guides and claw share one timing and alignment interface.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test a cube pinned diagonally and a delayed claw. Establish whether the collector can reverse without jamming the arm.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller drive, tunnel throat, sensors and cycle distributions.

subsystems.name: Positioning axes and claw
subsystems.construction: Older dossier describes a vertical belt lift, horizontal chain/rope extension and an articulated arm with shared claw.
subsystems.operation: Move joints together where allowed and use the same claw for scoring cubes and cones.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older account associates independent motions with rapid cycles. Exact component choices need team confirmation.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Quantify cycle improvement from motion overlap against peak current, deflection and stability. Presets must tolerate cube and cone seating differences.
subsystems.interfaces: The tunnel is a fixed receiver/sender interface. The arm and claw must visit it repeatably before travel toward the grid.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test one slow axis, a late homing event and recovery from a partially transferred cube.
subsystems.unknowns: Axis geometry, limit logic, stow envelope and deployed revisions.

subsystems.name: Cone acquisition and perception
subsystems.construction: Publisher identifies object detection. Inherited account describes Limelight correction for autonomous cone pickup.
subsystems.operation: Approach and take a cone into the claw directly, using a distinct recovery sequence if tipped.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older account reports a later preference for reliable station loading as loose cones became less available in advanced play.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An autonomous detector can help only if it resolves a pose early enough for the claw to reach it safely. The value of floor cone recovery depends on usable supply.
subsystems.interfaces: Vision adjustment, arm pose and chassis heading affect first contact.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test off-center and occluded cones, with a deterministic recovery if the detection is lost.
subsystems.unknowns: Vision code, station balance and chronology.

revisions: Separate ETR 19 from the team's COTS concepts. Older synopsis describes tipped-cone recovery and evolving station preference without installed dates.
transferable_principles: Compare both supply paths at the same gripper and measure the cost of waiting for handoff. Validate simultaneous axes under the worst loaded reach and current demand.
disconfirming_conditions: The wide collector and added axes lose value when handoff scatter or recovery time dominates, or when narrow lanes make the footprint a cycle constraint.
remaining_gaps: Team mechanism write-up or full captions, source code, exact axis layout and station sequence.
recommended_images: Team season photo and a source-linked cutaway or underside view of the cube tunnel and claw handoff.
